summary: A 1899 wooden lighthouse on Neil Head for a Cape Breton fishing cove; its first keeper was also an MLA. Recognized as a heritage lighthouse in 2015.

light.note: Headland light 851 in the Coast Guard list: white long flash every 6 s, seasonal. The breakwater light (850.6) is a separate red flash, Fl R 4s, 3 nm.

lens.note: Apparatus described in 1899 (as quoted by Lighthouse Friends); current apparatus not stated in the sources read

structures.note: Square, tapered wooden tower with sloping sides and an octagonal iron lantern. Register gives 10.4 m (34 ft); Coast Guard list gives 10.0 m.

staffing.note: Inferred: the keeper lost his job six days after the electric bulb was fitted (Lighthouse Friends); time clock from 1964.

access.note: Grounds open per Lighthouse Friends; reached by Lighthouse Road off New Haven Road, which leaves the Cabot Trail.

facts.ownership_note: Lighthouse Friends says the building was transferred in 2015 to the Neil's Harbour-New Haven Community Development Association, but its visitor notes still say the Coast Guard owns it.

events.note: Tower built 1899 for the fishing village
Angus A. Buchanan hired as first keeper, 14 August 1899, $150 a year
Hand-operated fog horn given to the keeper
George Sweet, Jr. replaced Buchanan as keeper
200-watt electric bulb replaced the oil lamp, 2 November 1956
Time clock switches the light; battery-operated 12-volt standby light for power failures
Recognized as a heritage lighthouse, 12 February 2015, under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act
Building transferred to Neil's Harbour-New Haven Community Development Association (per Lighthouse Friends; not confirmed elsewhere)
Rotten wood replaced and lantern room leak repaired with prize money from This Lighthouse Matters

corrections.why: The record's light values are the breakwater light's (850.6, Neils Harbour Breakwater Light). The tower light, 851, is listed separately with a different characteristic, height and range. The record also gives the breakwater's 2.8 m pole as a structure of the station.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register, Lighthouse Friends and the Department's table agree on 1899 and on Buchanan as first keeper (appointed 14 August 1899, table date Aug. 14).

The register and the 1899 description give 10.4 m (34 ft) for the tower. The Coast Guard list gives the tower structure as 10.0 m. The story reports both and says the sources do not explain the difference.

notes_for_editor: Sources: Lighthouse Friends (n2) is the main narrative and keeper list; it prints the Department's 1899 description, which is not in the local corpus (corpus begins 1900), so that description is second-hand and footnoted as printed by Lighthouse Friends. Table row checked on the page image (fact-check, 2026-10-27): the 1912 names table shows 'Neil Harbour | A. A. Buchanan | Aug. 14, 1899' on printed page 237 (scan page 244). The corpus's 'printed p.21?' for scan 244 was wrong, and the story now cites p. 237. A 1915 salary table (scan p.78 of the 1916 volume) lists 'G. Sweet Aug. 11, 1911' in an order that fits Neil Harbour, but it is matched by position only and is not cited. Walter Bragg's dates come from Lighthouse Friends only. No source read names the keeper for 1931 to 1936. Ownership: the 2015 transfer to the community association is stated only by Lighthouse Friends, whose visitor notes still say the Coast Guard owns the building; check before changing the record's 'federal'. The tower light's change from fixed red (1899) to white long flash (today) is not dated by any source read. The 2015 recognition date (12 February 2015) comes from the register copy at Heritage Guide; the Parks Canada statement page (dfhd id 14876) returned only its banner, so the register copy at HistoricPlaces was used. The keeper Buchanan is also the MLA in Wikipedia's article (1909 to 1914, died in office at Neil's Harbour): Wikipedia used as a lead only, and the death date is not in the story. The 'fire department' ice cream dates (1999 to 2003) follow Lighthouse Friends' wording ('had previously sold ... starting in 1999'). A Nova Scotia Archives photograph of the lighthouse (Clara Dennis collection, acc. 1981-541 no. 187CB) is credited on the register copy; its licence was not checked, so it is not in photos. Shape (fact-check 2026-10-27): the story has five chapters (The place, Building the light, The keepers, After the keepers, Today); the guide allows two to four for moderate evidence. Left as written for the editor to decide, since merging would rename chapters.
